transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... I guess I'm here because I've just kind of stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. 

It's probably nothing too serious, I just... well, things like salsa nights, or our church gatherings. I usually love cooking for the neighbors too, but I just haven't had it in me lately. I haven't even wanted to walk into my shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood, and I've been a carpenter for years. It just feels like I'm being a bit lazy, which isn't like me. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things right for you.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, let's see... I'd say it's been about two months now. It started right around the time my wife's health took a bit of a turn. It was sudden, and it just sort of upended our whole routine, you know? I mean, I'm sure it's normal to feel a little off-balance when things change like that, right? I just feel bad that I haven't been able to bounce back quicker. I'm really trying, I promise. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Have you also lost interest in things that usually bring you pleasure, or is it more that you're just not feeling up to doing them?

Well, gosh, that's a really good question... I, um, I don't want to make it sound like I don't care about my life anymore, because I really do. I'm sure if I could just get myself out the door to church or into the shop, I'd still enjoy it. 

It's just... I guess it's more that I'm just not feeling up to the effort of it right now? Like my battery is just a little drained, maybe. I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or being ungrateful for the good things I have. Does that make sense, how I'm explaining it? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since your wife's health took a turn?

Well... I guess I wouldn't want to use the word 'sad', because I really don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party for myself. But... I mean, honestly? Most mornings I do wake up with this... this really heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. It's almost like all the color has just drained out of the house, if that makes sense? 

I really try to keep a brave face, though. I have to force myself not to, you know, break down in front of my wife. She has enough on her plate right now, and I really need to be the strong one for her. I know I shouldn't be letting it get to me this much, and I feel terrible even complaining about it... I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that to you. Am I giving you the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm not trying my best to stay positive.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Well, I... I really wish I could say yes, because I know I should be keeping busy. But honestly... no, not really. And that's actually the main thing that brought me in to see you. I just... I've stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. 

I used to love going to salsa nights, or our church gatherings, you know? I'd even cook for the neighbors just to be neighborly. And my carpentry shop... I used to love just walking in there just to enjoy the smell of the wood. But lately, I just... I can't seem to muster up the desire for any of it. I feel awful even saying it out loud, because it sounds so lazy, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I want to get back to those things, I really do. Is it normal to lose interest like that when things get stressful? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past two months?

Well, um... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, my clothes still fit about the same, I think. I'm sorry, I haven't actually stepped on a scale lately to give you an exact number. I hope that's okay? 

I really do try to make sure I'm still eating, especially since I'm cooking for my wife. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health or anything like that. I know how important it is to keep my strength up right now. Am I supposed to be keeping closer track of my weight? I can definitely start doing that if you think it would be helpful for you.
Do you still enjoy the things you do manage to do, even if you don't feel like doing them most of the time?

Well... I guess that's the hard part to admit. Even when I do force myself to go out to church or... or step into the woodshop, it just feels flat. I used to get such a spark from it, you know? But now, even when I'm there, going through the motions, I'm just sort of... empty. 

I really try to act like I'm enjoying it, especially around the neighbors or my wife, because I don't want to bring anyone else down. I know I should be grateful for the things I can still do. I feel terrible complaining that it's not fun anymore... it sounds so ungrateful, doesn't it? I just... the joy just isn't there, even when I try my hardest to find it. I hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or not trying hard enough to enjoy myself. Is it normal to feel this disconnected even when you're trying to do the right things?
Are there any small pleasures in life, like tasting favorite foods or enjoying a warm bath, that you still find enjoyable?

Well, um... I really try to find the good in those little things, I honestly do. I know I should be appreciating a nice meal or a hot shower, and I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about everything. But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... even those little things just don't feel the same anymore. 

Like I mentioned before, that's really the main reason I'm here. I've just completely stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. The salsa nights, the church gatherings, cooking for people... even just stepping into my shop to smell the wood. I used to love all of that so much. And I feel awful that I can't even enjoy a favorite meal right now. It makes me feel like I'm not trying hard enough to appreciate what I have. Do you think I'm just focusing too much on the negative? I really want to be able to enjoy those small things again, I promise I'm trying.
Do you often feel guilty about things that wouldn't normally bother you?

Well, um... I know I shouldn't let my mind go there, and I really try to stay positive. I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party for myself. But... yes, I guess I have been struggling with that a lot. 

It's a little hard to admit, because I know I should be stronger for her... but I just keep replaying every single appointment we went to, and every little change in my wife’s health. I just... I keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner, you know? Like I should have been able to protect her somehow. 

I know it probably sounds completely irrational, and I hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or being ridiculous for obsessing over it. I just feel so responsible, even though I know I couldn't control it. Is it normal to beat yourself up like this when someone you love gets sick? I really do want to be a good husband to her, I promise I'm trying my best.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live or wishing you could just disappear?

Oh, um... well... I know I shouldn't think that way, and I really don't want to alarm you or make you think I'm giving up. I promise I'm fighting this. But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to admit this... it has crossed my mind. 

I haven't made any plans or anything like that, I swear. It's just... sometimes, when it's really bad, I've had these thoughts that maybe... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. Like, if I could just go to sleep and not have to feel this heavy anymore. And... this is the part I feel really awful saying... sometimes I catch myself thinking that maybe my wife and everyone else would just be better off without me dragging them down. 

It scares me to even say it out loud, because I know it's a terrible way to think, and I know I have so much to be thankful for. I feel so guilty even having those thoughts when my wife is the one who's actually sick. Please tell me you don't think I'm a horrible person for thinking that way. Is it... is it common for people to get so tired that their mind goes there, even if they don't really want to do anything? I'm trying so hard to stay strong for her, I really am.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound like I'm just slacking off at work, because I always try to be a hard worker. I don't want anyone thinking I'm getting lazy or anything like that. But... yes, I guess the guys at the shop have made a few comments lately. 

It's embarrassing to admit, but sometimes it feels like... like my boots are just filled with wet cement. It takes me forever just to walk across the floor and pick up a board. And then other times... I don't know, I just get so antsy. I'll catch myself just pacing back and forth around the shop, rubbing my hands together, and I realize I haven't actually gotten any useful work done at all. 

I know it probably looks terrible to the other guys, and I feel awful that I'm not pulling my weight the way I should be. I really am trying to push through it and stay productive. Do you think that's just because I'm so tired all the time? I hope you don't think I'm just using this as an excuse to not work hard. I promise I'm doing my best to keep up.
Have you lost any weight since your wife's health issues started?

Well, um... I really try to make sure I'm taking care of myself so I can take care of her. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health or anything like that. I know how important it is to keep my strength up. 

But, honestly, I haven't really noticed any weight loss. I mean, I haven't been stepping on the scale or anything... I've just been so focused on making sure she's eating and getting to her appointments. My clothes seem to fit about the same, I think. 

I hope it's okay that I haven't been keeping track of that. I know I should probably pay better attention to those things, and I promise I'll start monitoring it if you think I need to. Is it... is it bad that I haven't noticed? I really am trying to do everything right, I just... I guess my weight hasn't been at the front of my mind.
Have you lost any significant amount of weight unintentionally since your wife's health issues started?

Oh, um... you know, I think you might have just asked me about that, actually. I'm sorry if I didn't answer it right the first time. I really don't want to waste your time or make you repeat yourself. 

But, no, I haven't noticed any major weight loss... nothing unintentional, anyway. Like I said, I haven't really been checking the scale, but my jeans still fit the same as they always have. I really do try to eat, even when I'm not feeling up to it, because I know I need to stay healthy for my wife. I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I hope it's a good thing that I haven't lost weight. I'm really trying my best to keep everything together.
Do you feel like you're a burden to your wife and others around you?

Well, um... I really hope you don't think I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party for myself. I know my wife is the one who's actually sick, and I'm supposed to be the strong one for her. I try so hard to be strong for her. 

But... yeah, I guess I do feel like that sometimes. It's just... I can't stop thinking about everything that's happened. I just keep replaying every single doctor's appointment in my head, every little change in her health... and I just keep telling myself that a better husband would have noticed something was wrong sooner. Like, if I had just paid closer attention, maybe I could have caught it, or... or protected her from it somehow. 

I know that probably sounds ridiculous to you. I know I'm not a doctor. But I just feel so guilty that she's going through this and I didn't stop it. I try to make up for it by doing everything I can now, I really do. Do you think it's normal that I feel that way? I just want to be a good husband to her... I hope I'm not making things worse by feeling like this.
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is due to a lack of pleasure or a lack of energy?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm just giving up, because I promise I'm not. I want to be active, I really do. But... I don't think it's just about being tired. Physically, I think I have the energy, it's more that... I've just stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. 

I feel terrible even saying that out loud. Like, I used to love going to salsa nights, or church gatherings, or cooking for the neighbors... and I'm a carpenter, so normally, just walking into my shop to enjoy the smell of the wood is enough to make me smile. But lately, I just... I don't get any joy from any of it. I just don't have the desire. 

I know I should be keeping up with all of that, especially church and helping the neighbors, and I'm trying to push myself to care again. Do you think it's awful that I feel this way? I just really hope you don't think I'm intentionally neglecting my life... I'm really trying to get back to being the guy who loves those things.
Have you noticed yourself speaking more slowly than usual?

Oh, um... well, I haven't really noticed my speech so much, but... I hope it's okay to mention this, since you're asking about how I'm doing things. I really don't want you to think I'm slacking off at work, because I take a lot of pride in my carpentry. I always try to give my best effort.

But, well... some of the guys at the job site have made a few comments lately. They said I've been moving like my boots are full of wet cement. Like it takes me forever just to pick up a board. Or... sometimes I guess I just get stuck pacing around the shop, kind of rubbing my hands together, not really getting anything useful done. 

I feel so embarrassed even admitting that. I know I should be working harder, and I'm really trying to snap out of it. I don't want to be a burden on the crew. Do you think that's part of all this? I just hope you know I'm not doing it on purpose... I really am trying to keep up.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still when you're trying to relax?

Well, um... I guess that kind of ties into what I was just saying about work. I really hope you don't mind me bringing it up again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But, yeah, it's not just the moving slow part. Like I mentioned, sometimes I do get kind of... stuck. I'll just be pacing back and forth in the shop, rubbing my hands together. It's like I can't just sit down and take a break, even when I know I should. I just keep moving around, but I'm not actually getting any work done. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I know I should either be working or resting, not just wasting time pacing around. I'm really trying to get better at just sitting still and relaxing when I have downtime. Do you think that kind of fidgeting is something I should be worried about? I really want to be doing the right things to get back on track.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight since your wife's health issues started?

Oh, um... my weight? No, I don't think so. I really hope you don't think I'm letting myself go or not eating right because of everything going on with her. I know it's important to keep my strength up, especially now, so I've been trying my best to make sure I still eat my meals. 

I mean, I haven't actually stepped on a scale recently, but my work pants still fit about the same. So I definitely haven't lost five percent or anything drastic like that. I'm really trying to stay on top of taking care of myself so I can be there for her. Is it okay that my weight has stayed pretty much the same? I just want to make sure I'm managing all of this the right way.
Do you feel like your daily life has been significantly impacted by your current emotional state?

Well, um... I guess it has, a little bit. I really hope you don't think I'm just giving up or not trying to keep my life together, because I really am trying. But... well, I've had to hand off some parts of the jobs at work that I usually supervise myself. I just didn't want to mess anything up for the crew, you know? I want to make sure the work gets done right, even if I have to step back a little.

And, um... I guess I haven't been going to church as much, or seeing my friends and neighbors. I just... I didn't want to bring everyone down with how I've been feeling. I try to put on a brave face, but it got to the point where my wife and the contact from our parish got pretty worried about my safety. I feel awful that I worried them like that. I really didn't mean to. I'm trying to get back to being myself so I can be there for everyone again. Do you think it's normal to need a little step back like that when things get hard? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to fix this.
